Q: matplotlib savefig silently exits with code 1 after plt.plot() succeeds — no exception, no output A:

The issue is that you did not run conda activate bo-xgb before running ~/.conda/envs/bo-xgb/python.exe, so the environment variables like PATH was not populated by Conda, causing the Python process to unable to load the dynamic-link libraries with the correct versions.

Q: Discord.py error : [modal.py] Ignoring exception in modal <trainModal timeout=None children=1>: (modal.py:164) A:

So, for anyone who comes across this in the future, the error is handled inside the Modal class,
you can just search inside

discord.ui.Modal

for
Ignoring exception in modal

It happens when you don't handle errors yourself,

class trainModal(ui.Modal):
    async def on_submit(self, interaction): pass
    async def on_error(self, interaction: Interaction, error: Exception) -> None:
        await interaction.response.send_message('Oops! Something went wrong.', ephemeral=True)

which passes in the Exception object and relevant info.

Q: Which hotel has the most stayings? A:

which hotel has the most stayings[?]

Each visit corresponds to one row in table visited, therefore you want to count rows of visited on a per-hotel basis. That's this:

select tk_hotel, count(*) as visits
FROM visited
GROUP BY tk_hotel

If you want only the one (one of the ones) with the most visits then you can order the results by visit count, and take only the first. To get the name of the hotel instead of just its id, you should join the previous result to the hotel table:

SELECT h.name, mv.visits
FROM (
    SELECT tk_hotel, count(*) as visits
    FROM visited
    GROUP BY tk_hotel
    ORDER BY count(*) DESC
  ) mv
  JOIN hotel h ON h.id = mv.tk_hotel
WHERE ROWNUM = 1
;

Update

If instead you want all the rows having the maximum number of visits, then that's a different kettle of fish. Here's a way to express it:

WITH visit_count AS (
  SELECT tk_hotel, count(*) as visits
  FROM visited
  GROUP BY tk_hotel
)
SELECT h.name, vc.visits
FROM
  hotel h
  JOIN visit_count vc ON h.id = vc.tk_hotel
WHERE vc.visits = (SELECT MAX(visits) FROM visit_count)

Q: How do you find the disk size of a Postgres / PostgreSQL table and its indexes A:

Based on @aib's answer and @Ciges's improvement on materialized view and replace the source of truth from information_schema with pg_catalog, this will additionally include partitioned table as in the value p of pg_class.relkind. Also turn nesting sub queries into CTE.

WITH all_tables AS (
    SELECT s.oid::regnamespace schema,
           c.oid::regclass "table",
           s.oid::regnamespace || '.' || c.oid::regclass schema_table
    FROM pg_catalog.pg_namespace s
    JOIN pg_catalog.pg_class c ON c.relnamespace = s.oid
    WHERE c.relkind IN ('r', 'p', 'm')
      AND s.nspname NOT IN ('information_schema', 'pg_catalog')
), pretty_sizes AS (
    SELECT *,
           pg_table_size(schema_table) AS table_size,
           pg_indexes_size(schema_table) AS indexes_size,
           pg_total_relation_size(schema_table) AS total_size
    FROM all_tables
    ORDER BY total_size DESC
)
SELECT schema, "table",
       pg_size_pretty(table_size) AS table_size,
       pg_size_pretty(indexes_size) AS indexes_size,
       pg_size_pretty(total_size) AS total_size
FROM pretty_sizes
